description: Object decoding – fields, nested objects, key parsing, and §14.3 duplicate keys

tests.name: parses objects with primitive values
tests.input:
id: 123
name: Ada
active: true
value: null

tests.name: decodes a bare key: as an empty object, not an empty array
decodes a bare key followed by trailing spaces as an empty object
applies last-write-wins for duplicate sibling keys in non-strict mode
parses quoted object value with colon
parses quoted object value with comma
parses quoted object value with newline escape
parses quoted object value with escaped quotes
parses quoted object value with leading/trailing spaces
parses quoted field values that look like true or an integer
parses an unquoted field value starting with a bracket segment as a string
parses quoted object value shaped like a count-matching inline array header
tests.note: Quoting makes the value opaque (§4), so it is never parsed as a header – the matching count is irrelevant because a quoted scalar is never a header candidate

tests.name: parses unquoted values shaped like inline or tabular array headers after the key
tests.note: An unquoted key cannot contain a colon, so the first colon ends the key; a header shape in the remainder is value text

tests.name: parses quoted object value with bracket text and a later colon
parses quoted key with colon
decodes \uXXXX in quoted key (U+0004 control character)
decodes \uXXXX in quoted key (case-insensitive hex)
parses quoted keys with brackets and braces
parses quoted key with comma
parses quoted keys with inner, leading, and trailing spaces
parses quoted key with leading hyphen
parses quoted numeric key
parses quoted empty string key
parses dotted keys as identifiers
unescapes newline and quotes in keys
unescapes tab in key immediately followed by a colon
parses deeply nested objects with indentation
replaces a nested duplicate object key without merging in non-strict mode
applies last-write-wins for duplicate keys within a list-item object in non-strict mode
accepts unquoted key outside the encoder key pattern (hyphen)
tests.note: §7.3 constrains encoder output; decoders accept any token before the first unquoted colon as a literal key

tests.name: accepts unquoted keys with a leading digit or spelled like a literal or number as string keys
accepts unquoted hyphen-leading value in strict mode
tests.note: Encoders must quote hyphen-leading strings (§7.2); decoders accept the unquoted form as data

tests.name: accepts unquoted values and keys an encoder would quote in strict mode
tests.input:
k: b:c
paths[2]: C:\,D:\
a\: b
e: {}
tests.note: The first unquoted colon ends the key; the entire post-colon token is the value (§11.2)

tests.name: materializes __proto__, constructor, and prototype as ordinary own keys
tests.note: Decoding MUST NOT mutate the host object model, so the decoded object carries these keys as own entries

tests.name: materializes __proto__ opening a nested object as an ordinary own key
tests.note: The classic pollution shape – the nested object becomes an own entry, never the prototype

tests.name: materializes quoted __proto__ key as an ordinary own key
materializes __proto__ tabular field name as ordinary own keys
reads an NBSP before a quote, bracket segment, or nested field group as part of the name
tests.note: Whitespace is SP and HTAB only (§1.2); a leading NBSP keeps a line from being a keyless root header or a quoted key

tests.name: accepts a header key outside the encoder unquoted-key pattern
parses quoted empty string key opening a nested object
parses quoted key shaped like an inline array header
materializes __proto__ array header key as an ordinary own key
materializes __proto__ entry key as an ordinary own key
parses a key-value colon with spaces before it and a key-value or header colon with none after it
parses a quoted key followed by spaces before the colon
parses a hyphen-leading line outside a list as a key-value line
keeps keys that differ only in normalization form distinct
parses an empty unquoted key as the empty key
parses a hyphen-leading line off item depth as a key-value line or a tabular row
parses keys whose closed mid-token quote span hides a colon or a bracket segment, or precedes one
